decision: The existing synthetic-trained graph-proposal CNN is not ready for production or a hard MILP graph filter. Its corners depend on arbitrary A/B mask names, and visual review finds many proposals on smooth outlines and printed decorations.

summary.interpretation: Agreement between A/B label phases, not real junction accuracy or valid-template recovery.

syntheticForward.scope: Same CPU checkpoint through the historical and new input paths; not historical GPU-bit parity.

findings.finding: The whale, octopus and bird show substantial shifts or changed corner counts under phase exchange, despite identical photograph pixels and visible mask boundary.
Numerous proposed corners lie along apparently smooth petal, crescent and heart arcs. These are qualitative false-corner observations, not measured precision against annotated curves.

The CNN proposes corners on striped/dotted paper, printed trees/stars, letters and floral ornament. It does not reliably restrict proposals to transitions between sheets. The tree and ornamental flower demonstrate this even where the fixed material mask suppresses most of that ink.
Wrong fixed crops retain packaging, background or an oblique reflective fragment; proposals follow those structures too. This experiment does not alter the cropper.
Many clear grid corners and silhouette details do receive proposals. That potential usefulness coexists with false smooth-edge proposals; complete usable graph recovery has not been measured.

rootCauseEvidence: The same frozen model, RGB, valid pixels and exact binary boundary produce different fields when only mask label names change. This directly isolates phase dependence from cropping, photometric differences, fitting or training randomness.

The original checkpoint source hashes match the inspected model.py, train.py and data.py. The local detail branch receives the signed binary mask as a fourth channel; its architecture has no A/B-exchange constraint. Training applies joint spatial reflections, but no explicit mask-label exchange.
The phase dependence is therefore an unhandled model symmetry. The experiment does not prove that phase augmentation alone will remove false corners or improve reconstructed templates.
Printed-decoration proposals reveal a separate semantic failure: RGB corners are not necessarily material-boundary corners. Enforcing label symmetry alone cannot establish paper identity.
nextExperiment: Evaluate a fixed symmetric average of both phase predictions against the existing synthetic reference corners and boundaries, using unchanged thresholds and complete cohorts. It must preserve useful localization, not merely achieve phase consistency. Material-boundary supervision for printed paper remains a separate requirement.
limitations: The existing CNN saw procedural photographs, not this real development cohort.
These repeatedly inspected real photos are not an untouched holdout.
The mask itself can miss true material boundaries or contain printed-ink artifacts.
Phase stability is necessary for reliable proposals but does not prove useful graph connectivity or legal cutting paths.
Fields are stored in Float16, matching the historical localization evaluator. This diagnostic has no manually annotated real junction ground truth.
Native CPU times exclude image loading and processing and do not establish browser or mobile latency.
The deployed U2NETP crop fallback is a different network; its weights and production behavior are unchanged.
